messages:
irina: FYI customer reported sudden p99 spikes on hosted inference since ~09:00 UTC. They saw p95 ~120ms -> 220ms and p99 up to 1.8s. Customer trace attached in support ticket.

devon: Can you paste the support ticket/trace here? channel and model details please. Is this one tenant or broad?

irina: Customer is jordan-inc (multi-tenant request to hosted API). Model: gpt-neo-small-6b-quant. Route: /v1/generate. Happened across multiple hosts but concentrated on a few pools. Ticket excerpt:

```
RequestId: abc-123
Latency p50: 85ms
Latency p95: 210ms
Latency p99: 1798ms
Example payload: short prompt (~12 tokens)
```

sasha: Short prompts hitting high p99 usually points to batching hold window interaction with tiny requests. Could be microbatch hold-time building up for some hosts. Any config rollouts around 08:45?

devon: Checking deploy logs... opsbot, recent config changes to continuous-batcher? `opsbot deployments list --since 08:00`?

opsbot: Deployment log:
- 08:37: continuous-batcher: bumped default_max_hold_ms 50 -> 150 (canary group)
- 08:40: routing weight change for gpt-neo-small-6b-quant to new pool (canary)

irina: That matches timing. Customer spike at 09:00 after canary ramp. They said it affected ~5% of requests but severe tail.

sasha: Hypothesis: raising max_hold_ms increases microbatching for tiny requests, improving throughput but increasing tail when arrivals are bursty. For short prompts, holding longer to fill batches can push p99 when inter-arrival jitter is low.

devon: Need repro and metrics. Steps:
1) Identify host/instance IDs from traces
2) Pull continuous-batcher metrics: hold_ms distribution, batch_size distribution, queue_length
3) Pull per-host CPU/GPU utilization and kernel stalls

irina: Repro: jordan provided a curl test that spikes p99. They run 500qps of short prompts. I can run same against canary pool if we allow.

sasha: Run repro in canary namespace only. Use `--dry` flag to avoid billing noise? devon: permission to run stress on canary?

devon: ok to run localized synthetic load on the canary hosts. irina, run with these commands and gather metrics:

```
# generate 500 concurrent short prompts
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-small-6b-quant","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
done
```

Collect metrics from scribe: `metrics query "continuous_batcher{host=~\"canary.*\"}" --range 10m` and `trace lookup abc-123`.

irina: Ran repro. Observed intermittent p99 spikes up to 1.6s on canary hosts. Metrics show batch_size median 4 -> 10, but there are clusters where batch_size drops and hold_ms spikes to ~140ms.

sasha: That indicates late arrivals: the batcher waits full hold window for more arrivals, but sometimes very few requests arrive so single-request batches end up waiting ~hold_ms then go through -> tail latency. Also note scheduler priority: small requests didn't get expedited.

devon: Two immediate mitigations to try (quick config canary):
- Reduce default_max_hold_ms from 150ms -> 50ms for short-prompt route
- Enable small-prompt prioritization: route short_prompts to a tiny-batch fast lane (max_batch_size 2, max_hold_ms 20)

sasha: I prefer quick config change over restart. Patch config snippet below. We'll canary on 5% for 15 minutes then roll if good.

```
continuous_batcher:
  routes:
    "/v1/generate":
      short_prompt_policy:
        enabled: true
        max_hold_ms: 20
        max_batch_size: 2
  defaults:
    max_hold_ms: 50
```

devon: Plan:
- 09:50: push config to canary (5% traffic)
- 10:05: monitor p95/p99 and batch metrics for 15m
- If p99 drops to baseline (<300ms) and QPS stable: rollout to 50% then 100%
- If errors increase or throughput drops >8%: rollback immediately

irina: Pushed canary at 09:50. Initial 5m: p95 115ms -> 110ms, p99 1.6s -> 320ms. Batch size median decreased from 6 -> 2. CPU usage rose slightly (+4%) on canary but well within headroom.

jordan: Thanks for rapid response. We're still seeing a few 700-800ms spikes but much better than before. :thumbsup:

sasha: Good. Secondary improvement: consider adaptive hold where the batcher dynamically reduces hold_ms for route if average batch fill < 30% over window. I'll open a ticket for a feature flag.

devon: For longer-term: evaluate cost impact of increased small-batch processing (more kernels runs). Run a cost delta analysis across traffic profile.

irina: Customer updated ticket to confirm observed improvement. I'll keep monitor for next 24h and loop back with SLO/incident summary.

opsbot: Alert created: INC-2024-8472 assigned to eng-sre. Auto-attach metrics snapshot.

devon: Closing notes: root cause = config ramp (increase default_max_hold_ms) combined with short-prompt-heavy workload -> microbatch hold-time causing head-of-line wait for tiny requests. Mitigation = route-level short-prompt fast lane + reduce default hold. Action items:
- sasha: feature flag for adaptive hold (P2)
- devon: cost delta report (P3)
- irina: customer follow-up and close incident if stable (P1)

irina: Will update ticket and mark monitoring window. Thanks all.
